yam.resume: The bronze Sea of Shlomo: a large basin resting on twelve bronze oxen, three facing each cardinal direction, their hindquarters toward the center. Its rim is worked “like the brim of a cup, in the shape of a lily flower,” and two rows of gourds run beneath it — oxen, according to II Chronicles. The tour takes it from the First Temple and places it at the southeast of the building, between the steps of the Ulam and the ramp of the Mizbeach, next to the Kiyor of the Mishna.
cotes: ten amot from rim to rim
two rows of gourds (peka'im) beneath the rim (I Kings 7:24); II Chronicles 4:3 has two rows of oxen there, “וּדְמוּת בְּקָרִים תַּחַת לוֹ”
twelve oxen, three facing each wind, “וְכָל אֲחֹרֵיהֶם בָּיְתָה” — all their hindquarters toward the center
at the southeast of the building: “מִכֶּתֶף הַבַּיִת הַיְמָנִית קֵדְמָה מִמּוּל נֶגֶב”

sources.citation: מִכֶּתֶף הַבַּיִת הַיְמָנִית קֵדְמָה מִמּוּל נֶגֶב
שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה בָּאֶמְצַע, חֲמִשָּׁה מִימִינוֹ, וַחֲמִשָּׁה מִשְּׂמֹאלוֹ

yam.note: First Temple: I Kings 7:23-26; the Mishna does not mention it. Project's position: the tour places it in the Temple of the Mishna. Menachot 98b speaks only of the First Temple, where Moses' table and menora stood among Shlomo's ten (“שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה בָּאֶמְצַע”); extending this to the vessels of both Temples is the tour's choice. The two accounts also differ on its capacity: two thousand bat (I Kings 7:26), three thousand (II Chronicles 4:5).

mekhonot.resume: The ten mobile bronze stands of Shlomo. Each rolls on four wheels and carries a basin. Five are arranged to the north, five to the south, “on the shoulder of the building” — in the tour, the floor of the Azara along the body of the Bayit. Their panels bore lions, oxen and keruvim; in the tour, only their frames are shown.
cotes: four wheels of one and a half amot
a basin of four amot on each
five per side: “חָמֵשׁ עַל כֶּתֶף הַבַּיִת מִיָּמִין וְחָמֵשׁ עַל כֶּתֶף הַבַּיִת מִשְּׂמֹאלוֹ”
panels with lions, oxen and keruvim

sources.citation: חָמֵשׁ עַל כֶּתֶף הַבַּיִת מִיָּמִין וְחָמֵשׁ עַל כֶּתֶף הַבַּיִת מִשְּׂמֹאלוֹ
שֶׁל מֹשֶׁה בָּאֶמְצַע, חֲמִשָּׁה מִימִינוֹ, וַחֲמִשָּׁה מִשְּׂמֹאלוֹ

mekhonot.note: First Temple: I Kings 7:27-39; the Mishna does not mention them. Project's position, as for the Bronze Sea: the tour places them in the Temple of the Mishna. Menachot 98b, which sets Moses' vessels among Shlomo's, speaks only of the First Temple; extending it to the Temple of the Mishna is the tour's choice.

yakhin_boaz.resume: The two bronze columns of Shlomo, taken from the First Temple. A hollow shaft topped by a capital (koteret) worked in lily-form, encircled with lattice-work and chainlets, and adorned with two rows of pomegranates. They stand “לְאֻלָם הַהֵיכָל”: inside the Ulam according to Radak, Ralbag and Metzudat David, not in front of the façade. Yakhin on the right of the House (south), Boaz on its left (north).
cotes: twelve amot in circumference, that is four amot wide
capital of five amot: two flush with the shaft, three projecting
twenty-three amot in total in the model; twenty-two and a half according to Radak (on II Chronicles 3:15), half an ama of the shaft entering the capital
four amot of “מַעֲשֵׂה שׁוֹשַׁן” at the top of the capital
two rows of a hundred pomegranates per column (I Kings 7:20 and 7:42); Jeremiah 52:23 counts “מֵאָה עַל־הַשְּׂבָכָה”, ninety-six of them facing outward
Yakhin to the south (on the right), Boaz to the north (on the left)

sources.citation: לְאֻלָם הַהֵיכָל

yakhin_boaz.note: Adopted: the columns stand inside the Ulam — this is how Radak, Ralbag and Metzudat David read “לְאֻלָם הַהֵיכָל.” II Chronicles 3:15 and 3:17 say “לִפְנֵי הַבַּיִת” and “עַל־פְּנֵי הַהֵיכָל”: since the Ulam itself stands in front of the Heikhal, the tour sees no contradiction; their place on either side of the opening is the tour's choice. First Temple: I Kings 7:15-22; Middot does not mention them. The thirty-five amot of II Chronicles 3:15 measure the two columns together, lying down at casting, not the height of each (Rashi, Radak). The three amot of capital in II Kings 25:17 count only its worked part (Radak on I Kings 7:16).

mukhni.resume: The mechanism installed by Ben Katin at the edge of the Kiyor: a wheel that lowers the basin into its well every evening, “so that its water not be disqualified by the night.” The Gemara names only the wheel (Yoma 37a); the well comes from Rashi. The tour gives it a post, a crossbeam, a strut, a spoked wheel and a chain reaching to the edge of the basin.

sources.citation: שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיוּ מֵימָיו נִפְסָלִין בְּלִינָה
מַאי מוּכְנִי? אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: גִּילְגְּלָא דַּהֲוָה מְשַׁקְּעָא לֵיהּ
גלגל לשקעו בו בבור

mukhni.note: Tour's choice: the shape of the mechanism. The sources give only two features: a wheel (Yoma 37a) and wood, whose sound could be heard (Tamid 1:4). Post, crossbeam and chain are designed for the tour; no source mentions a chain.

magrefa.resume: When the kohanim reach the space between the Ulam and the Mizbeach, one of them takes the magrefa and throws it to the ground. In Jerusalem no one can hear his neighbour over it, and the crash serves as a signal: the kohanim come to bow down, the Levites to sing, and the head of the ma'amad stands the impure at the eastern gates (Tamid 5:6). It is a large utensil thrown to make a noise (Bartenura); Tosafot Yom Tov and the Rosh give it the shape of an ash shovel. The model lays it on the ground where it falls.
cotes: on the ground between the Ulam and the Mizbeach, where it is thrown
shaped like an ash shovel: a lid of thin metal, with a handle

מגרפות שנוטלים בהם הדשן, והן כמין כסוי הקדרה של מתכת דק ולו בית יד
הִיא אַמָּה וּגְבוֹהָ אַמָּה, וְקַתָּא יוֹצָא הֵימֶנָּה, וַעֲשָׂרָה נְקָבִים הָיוּ בָּהּ

magrefa.note: Adopted: a large utensil thrown down to make noise (Bartenura), shaped like an ash shovel (Tosafot Yom Tov, the Rosh). Set aside: the Raavad, cited by the Rashash, for whom it is the ten-holed musical instrument of Arakhin 10b-11a, all of whose voices were released at once. Tour's choice: its diameter, its handle and the bronze.

candelabres_shoeva.resume: The great golden candelabra erected in the Ezrat Nashim for Simchat Beit HaShoeva. Each bears four golden cups (sefalim) at its top and four ladders by which one climbs to pour in the oil. They rise far above the walls of the Ezrat Nashim.
cotes: four golden cups (sefalim) at the top of each

sources.citation: מְנוֹרוֹת שֶׁל זָהָב הָיוּ שָׁם, וְאַרְבָּעָה סְפָלִים שֶׁל זָהָב בְּרָאשֵׁיהֶן, וְאַרְבָּעָה סֻלָּמוֹת לְכָל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד

candelabres_shoeva.note: Tour's choice: the Mishna speaks of “candelabra” without giving their number; the tour raises four. They belong to the festival of Sukkot: the tour leaves them standing all year, unlit, and lights them only on the night of Simchat Beit HaShoeva.

shofarot.resume: Thirteen trunks “shaped like a shofar” — narrow at the top, wide at the bottom, so that no hand could be slipped in — lined up, in the tour, along the east wall of the Ezrat Nashim, on either side of the gate.
cotes: narrow at the top, wide at the bottom, so that no hand could be slipped in
along the east wall of the Ezrat Nashim, on either side of the gate
shofarot.note: Tour's choice: their material, bronze, which the Mishna does not specify, and their place along the east wall of the Ezrat Nashim, on either side of the gate.

sculptures_murs.nom: Wall Carvings: Keruvim, Palm Trees, Flowers
sculptures_murs.resume: The reliefs that cover the walls of the Heikhal and the Kodesh HaKodashim, taken from the First Temple: keruvim, palm trees (timorot) and blossoming flowers (peturei tzitzim), gold on gold. Ezekiel, who describes the future Temple, gives the order of the pattern — one timora between two keruvim, and two faces on each keruv. The tour arranges them in three registers, from one amah above the floor up to 22 amot, separated by bands of flowers. The keruv takes the form of the beings of Ezekiel's vision, whom the prophet recognises as keruvim: two wings covering the body, two more stretched out to meet the neighbour's above the palm, human hands and a single leg with a round foot.
cotes: three registers, from one amah above the floor up to 22 amot, separated by bands of blossoming flowers
“וְתִמֹרָה בֵּין כְּרוּב לִכְרוּב”: one timora between two keruvim
“וּשְׁנַיִם פָּנִים לַכְּרוּב”: two faces per keruv
on the walls of the Heikhal and the Kodesh HaKodashim, “מִלִּפְנִים וְלַחִיצוֹן”

sources.citation: וְאֵת כָּל קִירוֹת הַבַּיִת מֵסַב קָלַע פִּתּוּחֵי מִקְלְעוֹת כְּרוּבִים וְתִמֹרֹת וּפְטוּרֵי צִצִּים, מִלִּפְנִים וְלַחִיצוֹן
וְתִמֹרָה בֵּין כְּרוּב לִכְרוּב, וּשְׁנַיִם פָּנִים לַכְּרוּב
שֶׁכָּל הַבַּיִת טוּחַ בְּזָהָב, חוּץ מֵאַחַר הַדְּלָתוֹת

sculptures_murs.note: First Temple: I Kings 6:29; Middot 4:1 speaks only of gold, “שֶׁכָּל הַבַּיִת טוּחַ בְּזָהָב.” Ezekiel 41:18-20 describes the future Temple. Tour's choice: the carvings rise “from the ground to above the opening” (Ezekiel 41:20), that is, a little beyond the twenty amot of the Heikhal's entrance (Middot 4:1); above them the gold remains bare. The keruvim take the form of the chayot, “וָאֵדַע כִּי כְרוּבִים הֵמָּה” (Ezekiel 10:20): two wings covering the body and two joined to the neighbour's (1:11), human hands under the wings (1:8), a straight leg — “נראין כרגל אחת” (Rashi on Berakhot 10b) — with a round foot (Rashi on 1:7). Tour's choice: the four wings of the chayot given to the wall keruvim, which keep only the faces of a man and a lion (41:19), without features, and their wings joined above the palm. Set aside: a child keruv dressed in a robe — the child's face (Sukkah 5b) is said of the keruvim of the Ark. The three registers, the relief depth and the details of the motifs are designed for the tour.

chaines_devir.resume: Golden chains stretched before the Devir, the Kodesh HaKodashim. In the tour: three chainlets beneath the ceiling, stretched from one wall to the other, before the parokhet.
cotes: three chainlets beneath the ceiling, wall to wall, before the parokhet (the tour's choice)

sources.citation: וַיְעַבֵּר בְּרַתּוּקוֹת זָהָב לִפְנֵי הַדְּבִיר

chaines_devir.note: Tour's choice: the verse says golden chains run before the Devir (I Kings 6:21), without giving their number or height; the tour stretches three beneath the ceiling. An element of the First Temple, included like the Bronze Sea.

shaar_shushan.resume: The eastern gate of the Har HaBayit. Above it is depicted Shushan the capital, facing the Mount of Olives. The tour renders it as a bas-relief in the stone of the wall: a rampart and three crenellated towers.
cotes: above the east gate of the Har HaBayit, facing the Mount of Olives
a rampart and three crenellated towers (the tour's choice)

sources.citation: שַׁעַר הַמִּזְרָחִי, עָלָיו שׁוּשַׁן הַבִּירָה צוּרָה

shaar_shushan.note: Tour's choice: the Mishna says Shushan was depicted above the gate (Middot 1:3), without saying how. The bas-relief — a rampart and three towers — is designed for the tour, as is the gate's position on the axis of the Temple: Middot does not locate the gates within the wall.

tavla_helene.resume: A golden tablet donated by Queen Helena, “on which the parasha of the sota is written”: the Kohen follows it when writing the sota scroll (Yoma 37b). The tour places it on the gold of the east wall of the Ulam, on the north side.

sources.citation: שֶׁפָּרָשַׁת סוֹטָה כְּתוּבָה עָלֶיהָ
רוֹאֶה וְכוֹתֵב כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּטַּבְלָא

tavla_helene.note: Tour's choice: the Mishna does not say where the tablet was; the tour sets it on the gold of the east wall of the Ulam, on the north side. According to Reish Lakish in the name of R. Yannai (Yoma 37b), it bore the parasha only in abbreviated form, “בְּאָלֶף בֵּית,” and the Kohen writes “כְּמָה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּטַּבְלָא.” The engraved lines are decorative and do not decide the question.

beit_hahalifot.resume: The Ulam extends fifteen amot north and south beyond the body of the building, and these two extensions were called Beit HaHalifot, “because the knives were stored there”: Bartenura explains that large knives were called ‘halafim. Each projection is a closed room with two doors eight amot high: one onto the Ulam, the other, a wicket, in its western corner. Each of the twenty-four mishmarot — the teams of Kohanim who each came up to serve for a week (Rambam, Klei HaMikdash 4:3) — had its own niche in the wall for its knives. Sacrifices are slaughtered, a priori, with a knife from the vessels of the service (Rambam, Ma'aseh HaKorbanot 4:7), and those vessels are made of metal (Klei HaMikdash 1:13); when the neck is cut in a single stroke, the blade must reach past the animal's neck (Chullin 31a). Only one niche was walled up: Bilga's.
cotes: 15-amot extension: a 5-amot wall and 10 of space
two doors of 8 amot: onto the Ulam, and a wicket at the western corner

שני פשפשין היו בבית החליפות ופתוחין למערב

beit_hahalifot.note: Tour's choice: no source says where the west wall of Beit HaHalifot runs — the tour takes it out of the 16 amot so the body of the building stays 70 wide. The size of the niches, their place in the side wall, their order (that of the mishmarot in Divrei HaYamim I 24) are choices, as are the shape of the knives, their iron, their bronze handles and their number, two per niche. The Rambam (Beit HaBechirah 4:5) counts the Ulam wall and its ten amot within the hundred-amot width, as if they ran along the whole building; the Raavad disputes it (“שלא היה שם כותל לאולם כלל”). The tour follows Middot 4:7 and Bartenura: the fifteen amot project only at the Ulam. The tour follows Tiferet Yisrael (Yachin on Middot 4:7): each projection is a closed room, with its door onto the Ulam and its wicket in the western corner, eight amot high (Zevachim 55b), opening to the west (Rashi, citing the Tosefta). Set aside: Tosafot Yom Tov, for whom the projection is the Ulam itself, open; Rashi (Zevachim 55b), who puts the niches in the western wall, on the outside, and gives the name Beit HaChalifot to the court opposite. Width of the doors, partition, door leaf and the steps down to the Azara: choices.

niche_bilga.resume: Bilga is the fifteenth of the twenty-four mishmarot. The Mishna penalises it three times: it always divides its loaves on the south side, even on the day it enters service; its slaughtering ring is fixed, so it must borrow the others'; and its knife niche is walled up. The Gemara gives two reasons. Miriam, daughter of Bilga, had renounced the Torah and married a Greek officer; when the Greeks entered the Heikhal she struck the altar with her sandal: “Lukos, lukos — wolf, wolf! How long will you devour Israel's wealth without standing by them in their hour of distress?” The Sages penalised the whole mishmar, for what a child says in the market he has heard from his father or his mother. According to the other view, Bilga's mishmar was late in coming, and Yeshevav, who precedes it, served in its place.
cotes: the niche, the ring and the division of the loaves

sources.citation: בִּלְגָּה לְעוֹלָם חוֹלֶקֶת בַּדָּרוֹם, וְטַבַּעְתָּהּ קְבוּעָה, וְחַלּוֹנָהּ סְתוּמָה
מעשה במרים בת בילגה שהמירה דתה… כששמעו חכמים בדבר, קבעו את טבעתה וסתמו את חלונה
לְבִלְגָּה חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר
חַלּוֹנוֹת הָיוּ בְּלִשְׁכַּת הַחֲלִיפוֹת שֶׁשָּׁם גּוֹנְזִין אֶת סַכִּינֵיהֶם
וחלונה סתומה… כהיא דתנינן תמן הוא היה נקרא בית החולפות ששם היו גונזין את הסכינין

niche_bilga.note: Tour's choice: the Mishna does not say where Bilga's niche was. The tour arranges the niches in the order of the mishmarot, the first twelve on the north: Bilga falls on the south, top row. The niche is closed with a slightly recessed stone so that it reads as walled up.

cohanim.resume: An ordinary kohen serves in four garments of white linen: the kutonet, the mikhnasayim, the migba'at and the avnet. The kutonet falls to just above the heel and its sleeves to the wrist; the mikhnasayim reach from above the navel to the knee; the migba'at is a strip of linen that the sons of Aharon wind “like a hat”; the avnet, thirty-two amot long, is wound turn over turn at the height of the elbows. The kohen serves barefoot: nothing may come between him and the pavement. The tamid tour dresses its six kohanim this way: at the Kiyor, on the kevesh, at the altar's corner, on the altar and in the Heikhal — each has his own entry.
cotes: kutonet: to just above the heel; sleeve to the wrist, as wide as the hand
mikhnasayim: from above the navel to the knee
migba'at: sixteen amot of linen, wound like a hat
avnet: three fingers wide, thirty-two amot long, wound turn over turn
avnet worn at the height of the elbows
linen thread twisted sixfold; only the avnet embroidered with wool
the figures: 1.71 to 1.77 m, about 3.6 amot

sources.citation: וּמִגְבָּעוֹת תַּעֲשֶׂה לָהֶם לְכָבוֹד וּלְתִפְאָרֶת
וְאֶת הָאַבְנֵט שֵׁשׁ מָשְׁזָר וּתְכֵלֶת וְאַרְגָּמָן וְתוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי מַעֲשֵׂה רֹקֵם
וּבָנָיו צוֹנְפִין בָּהּ כְּכוֹבַע

לֹא יְהֵא דָּבָר חוֹצֵץ בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין הָרִצְפָּה
אַבְנֵטוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל זֶהוּ אַבְנֵטוֹ שֶׁל כֹּהֵן הֶדְיוֹט
מַנִּיחַ יָדוֹ הַיְמָנִית עַל גַּבֵּי רַגְלוֹ הַיְמָנִית וְיָדוֹ הַשְּׂמָאלִית עַל גַּבֵּי רַגְלוֹ הַשְּׂמָאלִית וְשׁוֹחֶה וּמְקַדֵּשׁ

cohanim.note: Adopted: an ordinary kohen's avnet is embroidered with wool, like the Kohen Gadol's — Yoma 6a discusses it, and the Rambam rules so (Klei HaMikdash 8:1-2). Tour's choice: the pattern of the embroidery, in stripes of blue-violet, purple and scarlet, which the sources do not describe, the exact shape of the migba'at and the figures' gestures.

leviim.resume: The Leviim sing standing on the Dukhan, each with his instrument; according to R. Eliezer ben Yaakov (Middot 2:6), the Dukhan stands on the step that separates the Ezrat Israel from the Ezrat Kohanim. Never fewer than twelve are counted: at least nine kinorot, two nevalim and a single tziltzal. In the days of Shlomo, the Tanakh shows the singers “clothed in linen.” The tamid tour places twelve of them, facing the Sanctuary, on either side of the axis one follows coming up from the Nikanor Gate; the free visit keeps only two, a kinor and the tziltzal, one on each side. At the tamid, Ben Arza strikes the tziltzal and the Leviim break into song: in the free visit as in the tamid tour, the tziltzal keeps the beat.
cotes: nine kinorot, two nevalim, one tziltzal
standing on the Dukhan, three half-ama steps (R. Eliezer ben Yaakov, Middot 2:6)

sources.citation: מַעֲלָה הָיְתָה שָׁם, וּגְבוֹהָה אַמָּה, וְהַדּוּכָן נָתוּן עָלֶיהָ, וּבָהּ שָׁלשׁ מַעֲלוֹת שֶׁל חֲצִי חֲצִי אַמָּה
מְלֻבָּשִׁים בּוּץ
וְהִקִּישׁ בֶּן אַרְזָא בַּצֶּלְצָל, וְדִבְּרוּ הַלְוִיִּם בַּשִּׁיר

leviim.note: Tour's choice: the Mishna does not say how the Leviim were dressed; the linen comes from the dedication of Shlomo's Temple (II Chronicles 5:12). The white kippa, the place on the top step facing the Sanctuary, the passage left open on the axis and the swaying are also choices. Adopted: the view of R. Eliezer ben Yaakov (Middot 2:6) — a one-ama step separates the Ezrat Israel from the Ezrat Kohanim, and the Dukhan stands on it. According to the first view in the mishna, the two courts are separated only by a row of projections (rashei pispasin). The Levite children, who stood below according to R. Eliezer ben Yaakov (Arakhin 2:6), have their own entry at the foot of the Dukhan in the tamid tour.

kiddoush_yadayim.resume: Before any service, the kohen sanctifies his hands and feet with the water of the Kiyor: right hand laid on the right foot, left hand on the left foot, bending over, according to the Rambam. The Torah makes it a perpetual law, “that they die not,” and a service performed without this washing is invalid. It is the first act of the morning tamid: the one who won the removal of the ashes is told “take care not to touch the vessel before you have sanctified your hands and feet from the Kiyor.” The tamid tour places this kohen south of the Kiyor, bent over his feet.
cotes: hands and feet together, bending over
right hand on the right foot, left hand on the left foot
before any service: the first act of the tamid
the Kiyor between the Ulam and the altar, drawn toward the south

sources.citation: וְרָחֲצוּ אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו מִמֶּנּוּ אֶת יְדֵיהֶם וְאֶת רַגְלֵיהֶם… וְרָחֲצוּ יְדֵיהֶם וְרַגְלֵיהֶם וְלֹא יָמֻתוּ
הִזָּהֵר שֶׁמָּא תִגַּע בַּכְּלִי, עַד שֶׁתְּקַדֵּשׁ יָדֶיךָ וְרַגְלֶיךָ מִן הַכִּיּוֹר
מַנִּיחַ יָדוֹ הַיְמָנִית עַל גַּבֵּי רַגְלוֹ הַיְמָנִית וְיָדוֹ הַשְּׂמָאלִית עַל גַּבֵּי רַגְלוֹ הַשְּׂמָאלִית וְשׁוֹחֶה וּמְקַדֵּשׁ
כָּל הַזְּבָחִים שֶׁקִּבֵּל דָּמָן… שֶׁלֹּא רְחוּץ יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם… פָּסָל
הַכִּיּוֹר הָיָה בֵּין הָאוּלָם וְלַמִּזְבֵּחַ, וּמָשׁוּךְ כְּלַפֵּי הַדָּרוֹם

kiddoush_yadayim.note: Tour's choice: the posture follows the Rambam to the letter; the Mishna does not describe it. His place south of the Kiyor, facing it, is also a choice.

aliyat_hakevesh.resume: One does not go up to the altar by steps — “you shall not go up by steps to My altar” — but by the kevesh, the ramp thirty-two amot by sixteen set against the south of the altar. All who go up to the altar go up by the right, go around and come down by the left, except for three services where one returns the way one came. The tamid tour has this kohen go up the east side of the ramp and down the west, in a loop.
cotes: kevesh: 32 amot long, 16 wide, south of the altar
up by the right, down by the left

sources.citation: וְלֹא תַעֲלֶה בְמַעֲלֹת עַל מִזְבְּחִי
וְכֶבֶשׁ הָיָה לִדְרוֹמוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ, שְׁלֹשִׁים וּשְׁתַּיִם עַל רֹחַב שֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה
כָּל הָעוֹלִים לַמִּזְבֵּחַ, עוֹלִין דֶּרֶךְ יָמִין, וּמַקִּיפִין וְיוֹרְדִין דֶּרֶךְ שְׂמֹאל

aliyat_hakevesh.note: Tour's choice: this kohen goes up empty-handed, to show the ramp and its direction; he carries neither limb nor vessel.

zerika.resume: The blood of the tamid, received in the mizrak at the slaughter, is carried to the north-east corner of the altar, then to the south-west corner: two applications “that are four,” each touching two faces of the altar. The rest of the blood is poured on the southern yesod. The free visit and the tamid tour place this kohen at the north-east corner, the mizrak in both hands.
cotes: the rest of the blood on the southern yesod

sources.citation: שָׁחַט הַשּׁוֹחֵט, וְקִבֵּל הַמְקַבֵּל. בָּא לוֹ לְקֶרֶן מִזְרָחִית צְפוֹנִית, וְנוֹתֵן מִזְרָחָה צָפוֹנָה. מַעֲרָבִית דְּרוֹמִית, וְנוֹתֵן מַעֲרָבָה דָרוֹמָה. שְׁיָרֵי הַדָּם הָיָה שׁוֹפֵךְ עַל יְסוֹד דְּרוֹמִית
הָעוֹלָה, קָדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים, שְׁחִיטָתָהּ בַּצָּפוֹן… וְדָמָהּ טָעוּן שְׁתֵּי מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע

zerika.note: Tour's choice: the kohen holds the mizrak before him, between two applications; the Mishna gives the corners and the order, not the gesture. The shape of the mizrak is also a choice.

melihat_haevarim.resume: “With all your offerings you shall offer salt.” The nine kohanim who received the limbs of the tamid carry them to the kevesh, lay them on its lower half, on the west side, and salt them: that is where a heap of salt sits on the ramp. The limbs wait there while the kohanim recite the Shema in the Lishkat HaGazit; they go up onto the fire only after the incense. The tamid tour places a kohen on the ramp, a foreleg in hand, taking the salt and scattering it.
cotes: lower half of the kevesh, west side
salt in three places: the Lishkat HaMelach, the kevesh, the top of the altar
limbs salted before the Shema, burned after the incense

sources.citation: עַל כָּל קָרְבָּנְךָ תַּקְרִיב מֶלַח
הָלְכוּ וּנְתָנוּם מֵחֲצִי הַכֶּבֶשׁ וּלְמַטָּה בְּמַעֲרָבוֹ, וּמְלָחוּם. וְיָרְדוּ וּבָאוּ לָהֶם לְלִשְׁכַּת הַגָּזִית, לִקְרוֹת אֶת שְׁמַע
בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת הַמֶּלַח נְתוּנָה: בְּלִשְׁכַּת הַמֶּלַח, וְעַל גַּבֵּי הַכֶּבֶשׁ, וּבְרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ
וְכָךְ הָיוּ מוֹשִׁיטִין לוֹ שְׁאָר כָּל הָאֵבָרִין, וְהוּא סוֹמֵךְ עֲלֵיהֶן וְזוֹרְקָן

melihat_haevarim.note: Tour's choice: a single kohen and a single foreleg, for the gesture; the Mishna lines up nine, each with his share — the second carries the two forelegs.

siddour_hamaarakha.resume: “The kohen shall burn wood on it every morning.” The ashes removed, the kohanim carry the logs up onto the altar to set up the great ma'arakha, on the east of the hearth, its face turned eastward. Any wood is fit except olive and vine; they usually took young branches of fig, of nut and of pine. The tamid tour places a kohen on the altar, a log in his arms, lowering it toward the pile before straightening up.
cotes: the great ma'arakha on the eastern side of the altar top, facing east
any wood except olive and vine

sources.citation: וְהָאֵשׁ עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ תּוּקַד בּוֹ לֹא תִכְבֶּה וּבִעֵר עָלֶיהָ הַכֹּהֵן עֵצִים בַּבֹּקֶר בַּבֹּקֶר
הֵחֵלּוּ מַעֲלִין בְּגִזְרִין לְסַדֵּר אֵשׁ הַמַּעֲרָכָה… כָּל הָעֵצִים כְּשֵׁרִין לַמַּעֲרָכָה, חוּץ מִשֶּׁל זַיִת וְשֶׁל גֶּפֶן
סִדֵּר הַמַּעֲרָכָה גְדוֹלָה מִזְרָחָה, וַחֲזִיתָהּ מִזְרָחָה

siddour_hamaarakha.note: Tour's choice: a single kohen; the Mishna says “they began to bring up the logs,” in the plural.

hatavat_hanerot.resume: The one who won the cleaning of the Menorah enters the Heikhal. If he finds the two eastern lamps burning, he cleans the other five — burnt wicks and ashes into the kuz, fresh oil and wick — and leaves those two; he then returns to the two eastern lamps: according to Tamid 6:1, before the incense, he cleans the eastern one and leaves the western one burning; according to the Rambam (Temidin 6:4), after the incense, he tends both. Before the Menorah stands a stone with three steps on which he stands; he sets the kuz on the second. The tamid tour places this kohen on the top step of the stone, facing the lamps; the kuz waits on the second step.
cotes: the kuz set on the second step of the stone
“when he trims the lamps”: in the morning, with the incense

sources.citation: בְּהֵיטִיבוֹ אֶת הַנֵּרֹת יַקְטִירֶנָּה

מִי שֶׁזָּכָה בְדִשּׁוּן הַמְּנוֹרָה, נִכְנַס וּמָצָא שְׁנֵי נֵרוֹת מִזְרָחִיִּים דּוֹלְקִים, מְדַשֵּׁן אֶת הַשְּׁאָר… וְאֶבֶן הָיְתָה לִפְנֵי הַמְּנוֹרָה וּבָהּ שָׁלשׁ מַעֲלוֹת, שֶׁעָלֶיהָ הַכֹּהֵן עוֹמֵד וּמֵטִיב אֶת הַנֵּרוֹת. וְהִנִּיחַ אֶת הַכּוּז עַל מַעֲלָה שְׁנִיָּה וְיָצָא
נָטַל אֶת הַכּוּז מִמַּעֲלָה שְׁנִיָּה, וְהִשְׁתַּחֲוָה וְיָצָא
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְפִיסִין פַּיִס שְׁלִישִׁי וּרְבִיעִי וְזוֹכֶה בַּקְּטֹרֶת מִי שֶׁזָּכָה וְנִכְנַס וּמַקְטִיר. וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִכְנַס זֶה שֶׁזָּכָה בְּדִשּׁוּן הַמְּנוֹרָה וּמֵטִיב שְׁתֵּי הַנֵּרוֹת

hatavat_hanerot.note: The shape of the kuz is a choice.

tzoarei_haleviim.resume: A Levite child enters the Azara for service only when the Leviim stand in song; he does not play, he sings, “to give flavor to the melody.” According to R. Eliezer ben Yaakov, the children do not count among the twelve and do not go up onto the Dukhan: they stand on the ground, their heads between the legs of the Leviim, and they were called tzoarei haleviim. The tamid tour places two of them at the foot of the Dukhan, in the Ezrat Israel, two and a half amot below their elders.
cotes: on the ground, not on the Dukhan
voice alone, without nevel or kinor

sources.citation: אֵין קָטָן נִכְנָס לָעֲזָרָה לַעֲבוֹדָה אֶלָּא בְשָׁעָה שֶׁהַלְוִיִּם עוֹמְדִים בַּשִּׁיר… רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר, אֵין עוֹלִין לַמִּנְיָן, וְאֵין עוֹמְדִים עַל הַדּוּכָן, אֶלָּא בָאָרֶץ הָיוּ עוֹמְדִין, וְרָאשֵׁיהֶן מִבֵּין רַגְלֵי הַלְוִיִּם, וְצוֹעֲרֵי הַלְוִיִּם הָיוּ נִקְרָאִין

tzoarei_haleviim.note: Adopted: R. Eliezer ben Yaakov, as for the Dukhan itself. According to the first view in the mishna, the children stand with the Leviim. Tour's choice: two children, on either side of the axis, in a linen kutonet like the singers.

shomer_levi.resume: The kohanim keep watch in the Temple in three places, the Leviim in twenty-one: five at the five gates of the Temple Mount, four at its inner corners, five at the gates of the Azara, four at its outer corners, and three at the chambers. The man of the Temple Mount makes his rounds with torches before him; a guard he finds asleep he strikes with his staff, and he may burn his garment. The free visit places a Levite outside the Nikanor Gate, on the steps, facing the Ezrat Nashim.
cotes: five at the gates of the Azara
the rounds of the man of the Temple Mount

shomer_levi.note: Tour's choice: the Nikanor Gate for this post, one of the five; the Mishna's watch is at night, and the tour shows him by day. His linen kutonet is a choice, as for the singers.

anshei_maamad.resume: “How can a person's offering be sacrificed when he is not standing by it?” The early prophets instituted twenty-four watches, and for each priestly watch a ma'amad in Jerusalem, of kohanim, of Leviim and of Israelites: those of the ma'amad in or near Jerusalem stand by the tamid, on behalf of all Israel; the others gather in their towns. Their place is the Ezrat Israel, the eleven-ama strip east of the Ezrat Kohanim, which they cross only for semikha, shechita and tenufa. The tamid tour places two of them, facing the Sanctuary, one wrapped in a tallit; the free visit, a single one, wrapped in a tallit.
cotes: Ezrat Israel: eleven amot wide across the 135 of the court
the Ezrat Kohanim is crossed only for semikha, shechita and tenufa

anshei_maamad.note: Project's position: the worshippers are not in period costume but in what their community wears today for Yom Kippur — suit and tallit, suit and kippa. This is a deliberate stance, not a reconstruction. The gestures are also choices.

kotel.resume: Today's Western Wall, where Jews pray. It is a section of the western retaining wall of the platform as Herod enlarged it: the Mishna's Har HaBayit of five hundred amot lies further east, inside. The midrash says the Shekhina never leaves the western wall and that it will never be destroyed; the Radbaz reads this wall as the western wall of the Azara, eleven amot behind the Kodesh HaKodashim.
cotes: above the plaza, seven Herodian courses with drafted margins, four Umayyad courses of smaller stones, then seventeen small Mamluk and later courses

sources.citation: לְעוֹלָם אֵין הַשְּׁכִינָה זָזָה מִכֹּתֶל מַעֲרָבִי

kotel.note: Choice of the tour: the Kotel is the wall of Herod's platform, not that of the Har HaBayit of Middot 2:1 — no verified rabbinic source identifies it with the five-hundred-amot wall. The Temple is set on the rock of the Dome, the Even HaShetiya according to the Radbaz (Responsa II, 691). Set aside: making the Kotel the western wall of Middot, which would put the rock under the Mizbeach, against the Radbaz. Choice of the tour: the height of the courses, which fills the nineteen metres; the count of courses comes from archaeology, not from the corpus.

place_kotel.resume: Today's prayer plaza at the foot of the Kotel, nineteen metres below the platform. Retaining walls surround it: the upper city stands above it. It has two levels: against the Kotel, the prayer area, dug out in 1968; to the west, the visitors' upper plaza, sixty centimetres higher, behind a low wall with a parapet that two gaps open. From its north-west corner a stairway climbs to the Jewish Quarter, and a covered passage leads to HaGai Street; to the north are the covered halls of Wilson's Arch; to the south-west, a passage towards Batei Machaseh; to the south, through the security checks, the way to the Dung Gate, and the Mughrabi Bridge climbing to the platform.
cotes: outline and stairway line from OpenStreetMap
the Jewish Quarter, twenty-two metres above the plaza (elevator project from Tiferet Yisrael Street)

two levels since 1968: the prayer area lowered by about two metres, then the step to the upper plaza reduced to sixty centimetres; the low wall between them, about ninety centimetres high, has carried a one-metre stone parapet since 1979 (S. Bahat, Cathedra 174, 2020)
the passages to HaGai Street, Batei Machaseh and the Dung Gate, and the gaps in the low wall, from OpenStreetMap
the furniture from OpenStreetMap: netilat yadayim stations, fountains, mechitza, low wall of the prayer area, fences, security checks, the "HaKotel HaMa'aravi" bus stop
a thousand white plastic chairs, delivered in 2020 (thekotel.org)
Aish HaTorah, facing the Kotel: seven storeys above the plaza (aish.com)
place_kotel.note: Choice of the tour: its level. The tour's thirty-metre terrain smooths the wall's nineteen metres into a gentle slope; the plaza is set at the visible height of the Kotel below its top. The stairway climbs in one flight, between two walls, to the ground the terrain gives at the end of its line; its steps are sixteen centimetres high. The furniture: height of the fences and low walls, a mechitza one metre eighty high, number and placing of the chairs, siddur shelves. The houses around it show it storeys of three metres twenty and arched windows: a pattern, not a survey. The tour's terrain puts its north-west corner — police, toilets, entrance to the Western Wall Tunnels — above it: their doors are brought to the foot of the nearest wall. That terrain puts the plaza itself thirteen metres too high: the three passages to the city stop after four covered metres, without saying at what level they reach it; their width of three metres fifty, their height, the one-in-twelve slope of the men's entrance and the steps of the women's are choices; the last stretch of the OSM low wall, along the slope, is not built. The upper plaza is laid flat.

esplanade_herode.resume: Today's platform, as Herod enlarged it. The Mishna counts only five hundred amot a side; the tour sets that square inside the present outline, the Kodesh HaKodashim on the rock of the Dome, and paves the rest at the same level.
cotes: level: the median of today's terrain inside the outline

sources.citation: הַר הַבַּיִת הָיָה חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת אַמָּה עַל חֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת אַמָּה
הַדָּבָר בָּרוּר שֶׁתַּחַת הַכִּיפָּה שָׁם אֶבֶן הַשְּׁתִיָּה בְּלִי סָפֵק

esplanade_herode.note: Choice of the tour: the Temple keeps the true east of Middot 2:4; the present outline is turned by six degrees, and its eastern wall runs about ten metres inside the north-east corner of the square. Nothing is built on it: the platform belongs to the Temple.

mur_herode.resume: The retaining wall of Herod's platform, on today's outline. It goes down to the ground, and rises above the paving where the city is higher than it, to the north.
cotes: parapet four amot above the paving (choice of the tour)
mur_herode.note: Choice of the tour: its masonry is that of the wall of Middot, for lack of another model.

arche_wilson.resume: North of the plaza, the covered prayer halls under the causeway leading to the Chain Gate. The Kotel continues there under a great arch springing from it: it once carried a bridge to the platform, above the street that ran along the wall.
cotes: span of the arch: thirteen metres
its crown: 6.1 m above today's floor
outline of the halls from OpenStreetMap
an ark holding more than a hundred Torah scrolls and a library, from the 2005–2008 renovation; the ner tamid, lit in 2010 (thekotel.org)
a shaft showing fourteen courses below the floor (Wikipedia)
arche_wilson.note: Choice of the tour: the vault is a semicircle running the whole length of the halls, and the rest of their outline is solid up to the platform's paving. The dimensions come from archaeology, Wilson's surveys included, not from a source of the corpus. The furniture and its placing: the ark at the far end, under the crown — against the Kotel the vault drops below one metre —, the library along the western side, the shaft near the entrance.

pont_maghrebins.resume: The wooden bridge climbing from the south of the plaza to the Mughrabi Gate, the only gate through which non-Muslims enter the platform today. Since 2007 it has replaced the earthen ramp that collapsed in 2004.
cotes: three metres wide, parapets one metre ten high (choice of the tour)
pont_maghrebins.note: Choice of the tour: the deck climbs in one stretch from the plaza to the paving, and the earthen ramp is cut down beneath it; the gate is a gap in the parapet of Herod's wall.

netilat_yadayim.resume: The two stations where one washes one's hands before entering the prayer area, on the upper plaza, by the low wall that closes it: taps and natlot, the cups that pour the water. An echo of the Kiyor, the bronze basin where the kohanim washed their hands and feet before the service.
cotes: location of the two stations from OpenStreetMap

sources.citation: וְרָחֲצוּ אַהֲרֹן וּבָנָיו מִמֶּנּוּ אֶת יְדֵיהֶם וְאֶת רַגְלֵיהֶם

menora_d_or.resume: The Temple Institute's golden menorah, on the stairway down from the Jewish Quarter to the plaza, facing the Har HaBayit: made to serve in a rebuilt Temple. Over two metres tall, half a ton including forty-five kilograms of gold, three feet and seven branches, in a glass case.
cotes: over two metres, half a ton, 45 kg of gold (joelfeld.com)

sources.citation: וְשִׁשָּׁה קָנִים יֹצְאִים מִצִּדֶּיהָ שְׁלֹשָׁה קְנֵי מְנֹרָה מִצִּדָּהּ הָאֶחָד וּשְׁלֹשָׁה קְנֵי מְנֹרָה מִצִּדָּהּ הַשֵּׁנִי

menora_d_or.note: Choice of the tour: its node. OpenStreetMap carries two, and the other falls inside a building's footprint. Its branches are curved like those of the menorah on display; the Institute made a second one with straight branches after the Rambam's drawing (Israel365 News), and that drawing is what the tour's Menorah in the Heikhal follows. The glass case is not modelled.

porat_yosef.resume: The yeshiva overlooking the plaza from the south-west, facing the Kotel. Moshe Safdie's building rises ten storeys from east to west; its stone walls enclose vaulted halls, and precast concrete domes crown it in series.
cotes: ten storeys, precast concrete domes (Moshe Safdie archive, McGill University)
porat_yosef.note: Choice of the tour: its ten storeys are counted from its foot, at three metres twenty; its openings and the spacing of its domes are a pattern, not a survey.

leviim_hamaalot.nom: The Leviim on the fifteen steps
leviim_hamaalot.resume: At Simchat Beit HaSho'eva, the Leviim stand on the fifteen steps that lead down from the Ezrat Israel to the Ezrat Nashim, with kinorot, nevalim, cymbals, trumpets and countless instruments, and sing. Fifteen steps, like the fifteen Songs of Ascents in Psalms. The rest of the year, the song of the korban is sung on the Dukhan, near the altar. On the night of Sukkot, the tour places fifteen of them, one per step, facing the Ezrat Nashim.
cotes: fifteen steps, from the Ezrat Israel to the Ezrat Nashim
leviim_hamaalot.note: Tour's choice: one Levite per step, their instruments and the way they face. The Mishna gives neither their number nor their place on the steps. The linen kutonet is taken from the singers of the Dukhan.

sources.citation: וְהַלְוִיִּם בְּכִנּוֹרוֹת וּבִנְבָלִים וּבִמְצִלְתַּיִם וּבַחֲצוֹצְרוֹת וּבִכְלֵי שִׁיר בְּלֹא מִסְפָּר, עַל חֲמֵשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה מַעֲלוֹת הַיּוֹרְדוֹת מֵעֶזְרַת יִשְׂרָאֵל לְעֶזְרַת נָשִׁים

tokei_hatzotzrot.resume: Two kohanim stand at the upper gate that leads down from the Ezrat Israel to the Ezrat Nashim, two trumpets in hand. When the gever calls — the rooster according to Rabbi Sheila, the Temple crier according to Rav (Yoma 20b) — they sound teki'a, teru'a, teki'a: the signal to go and draw the water of the libation from the Shiloach. They sound again at the tenth step, again on reaching the floor of the court, then go on sounding as far as the gate that leads out to the east. There they turn to the west: “and as for us, our eyes are to HaShem”. On the night of Sukkot, the tour shows them at the gate, before they go down.
cotes: from the upper gate to the east gate
tokei_hatzotzrot.note: Tour's choice: the upper gate is Sha'ar Nikanor, the only gate between the two courts. The trumpets of the tamid are silver (Tamid 7:3); the tour gives them that metal here as well, and their length is a choice. The descent while sounding is not shown.

hassidim_veanshei_maase.nom: The pious and the men of deeds
hassidim_veanshei_maase.resume: The pious and the men of deeds dance before the assembly with burning torches in their hands, and recite songs and praises before it. The Gemara records their words: “Happy is our youth, which has not shamed our old age.” The Bartenura adds that they juggled, with four torches or with eight, throwing one and catching the other. On the night of Sukkot, the tour makes them a ring of eight dancers, around the man with eight torches.
hassidim_veanshei_maase.note: Tour's choice: the ring, the number of dancers, their step and their place in the court. Like the tour's other worshippers, they wear what their community wears on festivals today. This is a deliberate choice, not a reconstruction.

shemone_avoukot.resume: It was said of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel that at Simchat Beit HaSho'eva he would take eight burning torches. He threw one, caught one, and they never touched. On the night of Sukkot, the tour shows the act without claiming to show the man: eight torches, four in each hand, each thrown again by the hand that caught it.
shemone_avoukot.note: Tour's choice: the figure is anonymous. The pattern is a fountain, each hand with its own four torches, never crossing. It is one way to make what the account describes possible. The rhythm and height of the throws are also choices.

sair_hamishtaleach.resume: The Kohen Gadol, in his four white linen garments, comes to the goat that will be sent to Azazel. A strip of crimson has been tied on its head, and it stands facing the gate through which it will leave. The Kohen Gadol lays both hands on it and confesses the sins of all Israel, pronouncing the Name as it is written. Then he hands it to the one who leads it into the wilderness. The Yom Kippur tour shows him with both palms on the goat's forehead, north-east of the altar.

כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל צוֹנֵף בָּהּ כְּמִי שֶׁלּוֹפֵף עַל הַשֶּׁבֶר
וְהַסּוֹמֵךְ עוֹמֵד בַּמִּזְרָח וּפָנָיו לַמַּעֲרָב וּמַנִּיחַ שְׁתֵּי יָדָיו בֵּין שְׁתֵּי קַרְנָיו
וּמַזְכִּיר אֶת הַשֵּׁם בְּכָל וִדּוּי מֵהֶן שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים… וּבְכֻלָּם הוּא מַזְכִּיר כִּכְתָבוֹ שֶׁהוּא הַשֵּׁם הַמְפֹרָשׁ

sair_hamishtaleach.note: Tour's choice: the Mishna says which way the goat faces, not where the Kohen Gadol stands. The tour places him against the goat's flank, facing the same way, his hands between its horns. The place north-east of the altar, the breed of the goat and the way the crimson strip is tied are also choices. The mitznefet is the same linen band as the priests' migba'at, wound flat.

korim_oumishtahavim.resume: When the priests and the people standing in the Azara heard the Name come from the mouth of the Kohen Gadol, they knelt, prostrated themselves and fell on their faces. They said: “Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom for ever.” The Rambam counts the Name ten times that day: three at each of the three confessions, and one at the lots. Full prostration, arms and legs stretched out, face to the ground, is permitted on stone only in the Temple. The Yom Kippur tour shows the priests in the Ezrat Kohanim and the Israelites in the Ezrat Yisrael, stretched out, heads toward the Heikhal.
cotes: kneeling, bowing, face to the ground
the Name ten times that day

sources.citation: וְהַכֹּהֲנִים וְהָעָם הָעוֹמְדִים בָּעֲזָרָה, כְּשֶׁהָיוּ שׁוֹמְעִים שֵׁם הַמְפֹרָשׁ שֶׁהוּא יוֹצֵא מִפִּי כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, הָיוּ כּוֹרְעִים וּמִשְׁתַּחֲוִים וְנוֹפְלִים עַל פְּנֵיהֶם, וְאוֹמְרִים, בָּרוּךְ שֵׁם כְּבוֹד מַלְכוּתוֹ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד
וּמַזְכִּיר אֶת הַשֵּׁם בְּכָל וִדּוּי מֵהֶן שָׁלֹשׁ פְּעָמִים… נִמְצָא מַזְכִּיר אֶת הַשֵּׁם בַּיּוֹם זֶה עֶשֶׂר פְּעָמִים
כָּל הַכֹּהֲנִים וְהָעָם הָעוֹמְדִים בָּעֲזָרָה כְּשֶׁהֵם שׁוֹמְעִים אֶת הַשֵּׁם הַמְפֹרָשׁ יוֹצֵא מִפִּי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל… הָיוּ כּוֹרְעִים וּמִשְׁתַּחֲוִים וְנוֹפְלִים עַל פְּנֵיהֶם
הִשְׁתַּחֲוָיָה זֶה פִּשּׁוּט יָדַיִם וְרַגְלַיִם עַד שֶׁנִּמְצָא מֻטָּל עַל פָּנָיו אַרְצָה
וְאָסוּר לַעֲשׂוֹת הִשְׁתַּחֲוָיָה עַל הָאֲבָנִים אֶלָּא בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ

korim_oumishtahavim.note: Tour's choice: the Mishna gives the three gestures, not the final pose. The tour freezes them stretched out, following the Rambam's definition. The number of people and their places are also choices. The Israelites wear what their community wears today on Yom Kippur, and go barefoot, like every worshipper in the tour.

bigdei_zahav.nom: The Kohen Gadol in the golden garments
bigdei_zahav.resume: The eight garments of the Kohen Gadol: the four of every priest — kutonet, mikhnasayim, avnet, headdress — and the tekhelet me'il hemmed with pomegranates and bells, the ephod of gold and woven wools with its cheshev, the choshen with twelve stones, the gold tzitz on the forehead. On Yom Kippur he wears them for the daily service: the morning tamid after the first immersion, his rams and the evening after the third and the fifth. The tour shows him so in the Parhedrin chamber, on the Water Gate and at the Beit HaParva, and nowhere else at the same time.

sources.citation: בִּגְדֵי זָהָב הֵן בִּגְדֵי כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וְהֵם שְׁמֹנָה כֵּלִים. הָאַרְבָּעָה שֶׁל כָּל כֹּהֵן. וּמְעִיל וְאֵפוֹד וְחשֶׁן וְצִיץ
לֹבְשָׁם בְּיוֹם עֲבוֹדָתוֹ וַאֲפִלּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת עֲבוֹדָה חוּץ מִן הָאַבְנֵט
פֵּרְסוּ סָדִין שֶׁל בּוּץ בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין הָעָם. פָּשַׁט, יָרַד וְטָבַל, עָלָה וְנִסְתַּפֵּג. הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ בִגְדֵי זָהָב, וְלָבַשׁ וְקִדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו
וְחָמֵשׁ טְבִילוֹת וַעֲשָׂרָה קִדּוּשִׁין טוֹבֵל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמְקַדֵּשׁ בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם

bigdei_zahav.note: Tour's choice: for the seven days in the Parhedrin chamber, no source says which garments he wears; the tour shows him in the golden ones, which he may wear on a service day even outside the service. The colours of the twelve stones, the cut of the ephod and the seat are choices. The avnet, tied under the me'il, is not shown.

bigdei_lavan.nom: The Kohen Gadol in the white garments
bigdei_lavan.resume: Four garments of white linen, the thread doubled six times: kutonet, mikhnasayim, avnet, mitznefet. The Kohen Gadol wears them only on Yom Kippur, for the service proper to the day. After the second immersion he puts them on for his bull, the lots, the incense and the blood brought into the Kodesh HaKodashim, then the scapegoat; he may also read the Torah in them. The tour shows him at each step in its place, only once at a time.
cotes: the service proper to the day

sources.citation: בִּגְדֵי לָבָן הֵם אַרְבָּעָה כֵּלִים שֶׁמְּשַׁמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל בְּיוֹם הַכִּפּוּרִים. כֻּתֹּנֶת. וּמִכְנָסָיִם. וְאַבְנֵט. וּמִצְנֶפֶת
וּפוֹשֵׁט בִּגְדֵי הַזָּהָב וְטוֹבֵל וְעוֹלֶה וּמִסְתַּפֵּג וְלוֹבֵשׁ בִּגְדֵי לָבָן. וּמְקַדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו וְעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדַת הַיּוֹם
אִם רָצָה לִקְרוֹת בְּבִגְדֵי בוּץ, קוֹרֵא. וְאִם לֹא, קוֹרֵא בְאִצְטְלִית לָבָן מִשֶּׁלּוֹ

bigdei_lavan.note: Tour's choice: for the Torah reading the tour keeps him in linen rather than in his own white robe. No figure enters the Kodesh HaKodashim: the machta set between the staves is enough there. The gestures and exact places at each step are choices, following the Mishna's indications.

zekenim.nom: The elders of the Beit Din
zekenim.resume: Seven days before Yom Kippur the Kohen Gadol is entrusted to elders of the Beit Din. They read the order of the day before him and say: “My master the Kohen Gadol, read it yourself, perhaps you have forgotten, or never learned.” On the eve they hand him to the elders of the priesthood and make him swear to change nothing of what they told him; he turns aside and weeps, and they weep too.

sources.citation: מָסְרוּ לוֹ זְקֵנִים מִזִּקְנֵי בֵית דִּין, וְקוֹרִין לְפָנָיו בְּסֵדֶר הַיּוֹם, וְאוֹמְרִים לוֹ, אִישִׁי כֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, קְרָא אַתָּה בְּפִיךָ
הוּא פוֹרֵשׁ וּבוֹכֶה, וְהֵן פּוֹרְשִׁין וּבוֹכִין

zekenim.note: Tour's choice: what they read, and how, the Mishna does not say; the tour shows two on a bench of the chamber, one with an open scroll. They wear what the tour's Israelites wear.

zikenei_kehuna.resume: On the eve of Yom Kippur, the elders of the Beit Din hand the Kohen Gadol over to the elders of the priesthood. They take him up to the upper room of the Beit Avtinas and adjure him, by Him who made His Name dwell in this house, to change nothing of all he has been told: “We are the messengers of the Beit Din, and you are our messenger and the messenger of the Beit Din.” Then they leave him. He turns aside and weeps, and they turn aside and weep.
cotes: the upper room of the Beit Avtinas
“we are the messengers of the Beit Din”

sources.citation: מְסָרוּהוּ זִקְנֵי בֵית דִּין לְזִקְנֵי כְהֻנָּה, וְהֶעֱלוּהוּ לַעֲלִיַּת בֵּית אַבְטִינָס, וְהִשְׁבִּיעוּהוּ
הוּא פוֹרֵשׁ וּבוֹכֶה, וְהֵן פּוֹרְשִׁין וּבוֹכִין

zikenei_kehuna.note: Tour's choice: two elders, east of the mortar, and he at the window over the Azara; the hand over the eyes. Off duty, they wear what the tour's Israelites wear.

sadin_shel_butz.resume: At each immersion a sheet of fine linen is spread between the Kohen Gadol and the people. Behind it he undresses, goes down to immerse, comes up, dries himself, puts on the garments brought to him and sanctifies his hands and feet. The first time above the Water Gate, the others on the roof of the Beit HaParva.

sources.citation: פֵּרְסוּ סָדִין שֶׁל בּוּץ בֵּינוֹ לְבֵין הָעָם. פָּשַׁט, יָרַד וְטָבַל, עָלָה וְנִסְתַּפֵּג. הֵבִיאוּ לוֹ בִגְדֵי זָהָב, וְלָבַשׁ וְקִדֵּשׁ יָדָיו וְרַגְלָיו

sadin_shel_butz.note: Tour's choice: who holds it, and how high, the Mishna does not say. The tour has two priests stretch it at shoulder height: the Kohen Gadol's head, in the headdress of the moment, shows above it.

goral.nom: The deputy and the head of the house at the lots
goral.resume: At the lots, in the east of the Azara, north of the altar, the deputy stands at the Kohen Gadol's right, the head of the father's house at his left. He shakes the urn and draws the two lots, one in each hand. If the one for the Name comes up in his right, the deputy tells him: “My master the Kohen Gadol, raise your right”; in the left, the head of the house tells him.
cotes: the head of the house at the left

sources.citation: טָרַף בַּקַּלְפִּי וְהֶעֱלָה שְׁנֵי גוֹרָלוֹת… הַסְּגָן בִּימִינוֹ וְרֹאשׁ בֵּית אָב מִשְּׂמֹאלוֹ
הֵיכָן מַגְרִיל. בְּמִזְרַח הָעֲזָרָה בִּצְפוֹן הַמִּזְבֵּחַ… וּשְׁנֵי הַשְּׂעִירִים לְפָנָיו אֶחָד לִימִינוֹ וְאֶחָד לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ

goral.note: Tour's choice: their age, gestures and spacing. The kalpi stands on a pedestal, and the lot for the Name comes up in the right hand: also choices.

keriat_hatorah.nom: Those who pass him the scroll
keriat_hatorah.resume: For the Kohen Gadol's reading, the scroll passes from hand to hand in order of honour: the synagogue attendant takes it and gives it to the head of the synagogue, who gives it to the deputy, who gives it to the Kohen Gadol. Standing, he receives it and reads. The three stay near him during the reading.

sources.citation: חַזַּן הַכְּנֶסֶת נוֹטֵל סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה וְנוֹתְנוֹ לְרֹאשׁ הַכְּנֶסֶת, וְרֹאשׁ הַכְּנֶסֶת נוֹתְנוֹ לַסְּגָן, וְהַסְּגָן נוֹתְנוֹ לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, וְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל עוֹמֵד וּמְקַבֵּל וְקוֹרֵא

keriat_hatorah.note: Tour's choice: their place during the reading, their age and dress. The deputy is dressed as a priest; the attendant and the head of the synagogue like the tour's Israelites.

kat_shniya.resume: The pesach is slaughtered in three groups, one after another. The first enters, the Azara fills and its doors are locked; when it has finished offering, they are opened again, it goes out and the second enters, then the third. Rabbi Yitzchak: three groups of thirty men each — kahal, edah, Israel.

sources.citation: יָצְתָה כַת רִאשׁוֹנָה וְנִכְנְסָה כַת שְׁנִיָּה. יָצְתָה שְׁנִיָּה, נִכְנְסָה שְׁלִישִׁית
שָׁלְמוּ מִלְּהַקְרִיב פּוֹתְחִין דַּלְתוֹת הָעֲזָרָה וְיוֹצֵאת כַּת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה וְנִכְנְסָה שְׁנִיָּה
אֵין הַפֶּסַח נִשְׁחָט אֶלָּא בְּשָׁלֹשׁ כִּתּוֹת שֶׁל שְׁלֹשִׁים שְׁלֹשִׁים בְּנֵי אָדָם
שֶׂה תָמִים זָכָר בֶּן שָׁנָה יִהְיֶה לָכֶם מִן הַכְּבָשִׂים וּמִן הָעִזִּים תִּקָּחוּ

kat_shniya.note: Tour's choice: the waiting in the Ezrat Nashim and a lamb beside each man, its breed and fleece; the Torah allows a lamb or a kid. The Nikanor gate stays open, as throughout the tour, although the Mishnah has it closed while the first group is inside — by itself according to Abaye, closed by people according to Rava (Pesachim 64b).

bazikhin.resume: The kohanim stand in rows, bazikhin in hand — large cups to receive the blood: a row all of silver, a row all of gold, never mixed. The full bazikh passes from hand to hand to the altar, and one takes the full one before returning the empty. They had no base: wide at the top, pointed below, they could not be set on the ground, where the blood would have congealed.

sources.citation: הַכֹּהֲנִים עוֹמְדִים שׁוּרוֹת שׁוּרוֹת, וּבִידֵיהֶם בָּזִיכֵי כֶסֶף וּבָזִיכֵי זָהָב. שׁוּרָה שֶׁכֻּלָּהּ כֶּסֶף כֶּסֶף, וְשׁוּרָה שֶׁכֻּלָּהּ זָהָב זָהָב. לֹא הָיוּ מְעֹרָבִין. וְלֹא הָיוּ לַבָּזִיכִין שׁוּלַיִם, שֶׁמָּא יַנִּיחוּם וְיִקְרַשׁ הַדָּם
נוֹתְנוֹ לַחֲבֵרוֹ וַחֲבֵרוֹ לַחֲבֵרוֹ, וּמְקַבֵּל אֶת הַמָּלֵא וּמַחֲזִיר אֶת הָרֵיקָן
בָּזִיכֵי. כַּפּוֹת גְּדוֹלוֹת לְקַבֵּל בָּהֶם הַדָּם… דְּהָכִי שַׁפִּיר טְפֵי… רְחָבִים הָיוּ מִלְמַעְלָה וְתַחְתֵּיהֶם חַדִּים, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יוּכְלוּ לֵישֵׁב עַל הַקַּרְקַע
וְלֹא הָיוּ מְעֹרָבִים כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לָהֶם נוֹי

bazikhin.note: Tour's choice: two rows of four, facing each other, running from the place of slaughter to the north of the altar. The Mishnah gives neither their number nor their place; the pesach may be slaughtered anywhere in the Azara (Zevachim 5:8). The profile of the bazikhin is also a choice.

shechitat_hapessah.nom: The slaughter and the throwing of the pesach
shechitat_hapessah.resume: An Israelite slaughters: slaughter is valid when done by a non-kohen. The kohen receives the blood in a bazikh, and the blood passes from hand to hand to the kohen nearest the altar, who throws it in a single throw toward the yesod; the pesach needs only one application.

sources.citation: שָׁחַט יִשְׂרָאֵל וְקִבֵּל הַכֹּהֵן, נוֹתְנוֹ לַחֲבֵרוֹ וַחֲבֵרוֹ לַחֲבֵרוֹ… כֹּהֵן הַקָּרוֹב אֵצֶל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ זוֹרְקוֹ זְרִיקָה אַחַת כְּנֶגֶד הַיְסוֹד
הַבְּכוֹר וְהַמַּעֲשֵׂר וְהַפֶּסַח… שְׁחִיטָתָן בְּכָל מָקוֹם בָּעֲזָרָה, וְדָמָן טָעוּן מַתָּנָה אַחַת, וּבִלְבָד שֶׁיִּתֵּן כְּנֶגֶד הַיְסוֹד
כָּל הַפְּסוּלִין שֶׁשָּׁחֲטוּ, שְׁחִיטָתָן כְּשֵׁרָה. שֶׁהַשְּׁחִיטָה כְשֵׁרָה בְּזָרִים

shechitat_hapessah.note: Tour's choice: the place of slaughter, north of the rows; the lamb lying on its side, the knife and the gestures; the kohen who throws, facing the northern yesod.

hallel_bepessah.resume: While they slaughter and offer, the Levites read the Hallel; if they finish, they repeat it, and a third time if need be — which never happened. At each reading the trumpets sound three times: teki'a, teru'a, teki'a; the pesach has no libation, at which one usually sounds, so one sounds at the slaughter. The flute plays before the altar.

sources.citation: קָרְאוּ אֶת הַהַלֵּל. אִם גָּמְרוּ שָׁנוּ, וְאִם שָׁנוּ שִׁלְּשׁוּ, אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא שִׁלְּשׁוּ מִימֵיהֶם
וְכָל זְמַן שֶׁהֵן שׁוֹחֲטִין וּמַקְרִיבִין קוֹרְאִים הַלְּוִיִּים אֶת הַהַלֵּל
עַל כָּל קְרִיאָה וּקְרִיאָה תּוֹקְעִין שָׁלֹשׁ תְּקִיעוֹת בַּחֲצוֹצְרוֹת… הוֹאִיל וְאֵין לוֹ נְסָכִים לִתְקֹעַ בִּשְׁעַת נִסּוּךְ תּוֹקְעִין בִּשְׁעַת שְׁחִיטָה
וּבִשְׁנֵים עָשָׂר יוֹם בַּשָּׁנָה הֶחָלִיל מַכֶּה לִפְנֵי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ. בִּשְׁחִיטַת פֶּסַח רִאשׁוֹן

hallel_bepessah.note: Tour's choice: the twelve Levites on the Dukhan with their instruments, as at the tamid; two kohanim with trumpets at the foot of the Dukhan. The flute is not shown.

tolin_umafshitin.resume: Iron hooks are fixed in the walls and in the pillars: on them the pesach is hung and flayed. Whoever has no room takes one of the thin, smooth rods kept there, lays it on his own shoulder and his fellow's, hangs the animal on it and flays it. Rabbi Eliezer: when the fourteenth falls on Shabbat, each lays his hand on the other's shoulder.

sources.citation: אֻנְקְלָיוֹת שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל הָיוּ קְבוּעִים בַּכְּתָלִים וּבָעַמּוּדִים, שֶׁבָּהֶן תּוֹלִין וּמַפְשִׁיטִין. וְכָל מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ מָקוֹם לִתְלוֹת וּלְהַפְשִׁיט, מַקְלוֹת דַּקִּים חֲלָקִים הָיוּ שָׁם, וּמֵנִיחַ עַל כְּתֵפוֹ וְעַל כֶּתֶף חֲבֵרוֹ, וְתוֹלֶה וּמַפְשִׁיט
וְעָלָיו שְׁמֹנָה עַמּוּדִים נַנָּסִין, וּרְבִיעִין שֶׁל אֶרֶז עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן, וְאֻנְקְלָיוֹת שֶׁל בַּרְזֶל הָיוּ קְבוּעִין בָּהֶם

tolin_umafshitin.note: Tour's choice: a lamb on the hook of a pillar of the Beit HaMitbachayim, and two men with a rod a little to the west; Israelites do the flaying, and their gestures are also a choice.

magis.resume: The pesach is opened and its emurim — the fats that go up on the altar — are taken out and put in a dish, the magis, and the kohen salts them and burns them on the altar.

sources.citation: קְרָעוֹ וְהוֹצִיא אֵמוּרָיו, נְתָנוֹ בְמָגִיס וְהִקְטִירָן עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ
אֵמוּרָיו. הַחֲלָבִים הַקְּרֵבִים עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ. בְּמָגִיס. בִּקְעָרָה
וּמוֹצִיא אֶת הָאֵימוּרִין וְנוֹתְנָן בִּכְלִי וּמוֹלְחָן וּמַקְטִירָן הַכֹּהֵן עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ

magis.note: Tour's choice: the magis, a deep silver dish; the kohen at the edge of the great ma'arakha, tilting the dish toward the fire.

yoshvim_bacheil.nom: The second group, sitting in the Cheil
yoshvim_bacheil.resume: When 14 Nisan falls on Shabbat, no one carries his pesach home: the first group sits on the Har HaBayit, the second in the Cheil, between the Soreg and the wall of the Ezrat Nashim, and the third stays standing in its place, in the Azara, until Shabbat ends. Each puts his pesach in its skin and slings it over his back.
cotes: the last step of the Cheil

sources.citation: יָצְתָה כַת רִאשׁוֹנָה וְיָשְׁבָה לָהּ בְּהַר הַבַּיִת, שְׁנִיָּה בַּחֵיל, וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁית בִּמְקוֹמָהּ עוֹמֶדֶת. חֲשֵׁכָה, יָצְאוּ וְצָלוּ אֶת פִּסְחֵיהֶן
יָשְׁבָה לָהּ בְּהַר הַבַּיִת. בְּשַׁבָּת קָאָמַר… בַּחֵיל. בֵּין הַסּוֹרֵג לְחוֹמַת הָעֲזָרָה שֶׁל נָשִׁים
אֵין כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מוֹלִיךְ אֶת פִּסְחוֹ לְבֵיתוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת… וְשׁוֹהִים הַכּל עַד מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת
כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד נוֹתֵן פִּסְחוֹ בְּעוֹרוֹ, וּמַפְשִׁיל לַאֲחוֹרָיו

yoshvim_bacheil.note: Tour's choice: they sit on the last step of the Cheil, the pesach lying beside each rather than slung over his back.

maalei_bikkourim.nom: Those who bring up the bikkurim
maalei_bikkourim.resume: The towns of the ma'amad gather in its town, and in the morning the officer says: “Arise, let us go up to Zion, to the house of HaShem our God.” Those nearby bring fresh figs and grapes, those far away dried figs and raisins. The ox walks before them, its horns overlaid with gold, a crown of olive on its head. At the Har HaBayit each takes the basket on his own shoulder — even King Agrippas — and goes in as far as the Azara.

sources.citation: וְלַמַּשְׁכִּים, הָיָה הַמְמֻנֶּה אוֹמֵר, קוּמוּ וְנַעֲלֶה צִיּוֹן אֶל בֵּית ה' אֱלֹהֵינוּ
וְהַשּׁוֹר הוֹלֵךְ לִפְנֵיהֶם, וְקַרְנָיו מְצֻפּוֹת זָהָב, וַעֲטֶרֶת שֶׁל זַיִת בְּרֹאשׁוֹ
הִגִּיעוּ לְהַר הַבַּיִת, אֲפִלּוּ אַגְרִיפַּס הַמֶּלֶךְ נוֹטֵל הַסַּל עַל כְּתֵפוֹ וְנִכְנָס, עַד שֶׁמַּגִּיעַ לָעֲזָרָה
הִגִּיעַ לְהַר הַבַּיִת נוֹטֵל הַסַּל עַל כְּתֵפוֹ הוּא בְּעַצְמוֹ. וַאֲפִלּוּ הָיָה מֶלֶךְ גָּדוֹל שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל

maalei_bikkourim.note: Tour's choice: the number of bearers and their place; who carries a plated basket, who a wicker one; the ox on the Har HaBayit, its coat, the weave of the crown. The flute plays before them “until they reach the Har HaBayit” (3:4): it is not shown.

shir_habikkourim.resume: As soon as the bearers reach the Azara, the Levites begin the song: “I will extol You, HaShem, for You have lifted me up, and have not let my enemies rejoice over me.” The bikkurim require song, as they require waving and a shelamim offering.

sources.citation: הִגִּיעַ לָעֲזָרָה וְדִבְּרוּ הַלְוִיִּם בַּשִּׁיר, אֲרוֹמִמְךָ ה' כִּי דִלִּיתָנִי וְלֹא שִׂמַּחְתָּ אֹיְבַי לִי
מִשֶּׁיַּגִּיעוּ לַעֲזָרָה הַלְוִיִּם הָיוּ מַתְחִילִין וְקוֹרִין
וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁטְּעוּנִין תְּנוּפָה כָּךְ טְעוּנִין קָרְבַּן שְׁלָמִים [וְשִׁיר]
אֲרוֹמִמְךָ ה' כִּי דִלִּיתָנִי וְלֹא שִׂמַּחְתָּ אֹיְבַי לִי

shir_habikkourim.note: Tour's choice: the twelve Levites on the Dukhan with the instruments of the tamid; two bearers entering the Ezrat Israel.

mikra_bikkourim.resume: With the basket still on his shoulder, the bearer says to the kohen “I declare today to HaShem your God that I have come into the land” (Deuteronomy 26:3), and reads up to “Arami oved avi”. At first, whoever could read read, and whoever could not was prompted; people then held back from bringing, so it was instituted that everyone be prompted, whether he knows how or not.
cotes: the basket still on his shoulder

sources.citation: עוֹדֵהוּ הַסַּל עַל כְּתֵפוֹ, קוֹרֵא מֵהִגַּדְתִּי הַיּוֹם לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ
וּבָאתָ אֶל הַכֹּהֵן אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם וְאָמַרְתָּ אֵלָיו הִגַּדְתִּי הַיּוֹם לַה' אֱלֹהֶיךָ

בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה, כָּל מִי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ לִקְרוֹת, קוֹרֵא. וְכָל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ לִקְרוֹת, מַקְרִין אוֹתוֹ. נִמְנְעוּ מִלְּהָבִיא, הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ מַקְרִין אֶת מִי שֶׁיּוֹדֵעַ וְאֶת מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ

mikra_bikkourim.note: Tour's choice: the place of the reading, near the south-west horn where the basket will be set down; the kohen listening; two bearers waiting. The one who prompts is not shown.

tenoufat_bikkourim.resume: Reaching “Arami oved avi”, the bearer lowers the basket from his shoulder and holds it by its rim; the kohen puts his hand beneath it and waves it — forward and back, up and down —, and the bearer reads to the end of the passage. One may wave even east of the altar, all the more so to its west. For the waving, the Israelite enters the Ezrat Kohanim.
cotes: the basket held by its rim

sources.citation: הִגִּיעַ לַאֲרַמִּי אֹבֵד אָבִי, מוֹרִיד הַסַּל מֵעַל כְּתֵפוֹ וְאוֹחֲזוֹ בְשִׂפְתוֹתָיו, וְכֹהֵן מַנִּיחַ יָדוֹ תַחְתָּיו וּמְנִיפוֹ
מוֹלִיךְ וּמֵבִיא, מַעֲלֶה וּמוֹרִיד
אַף בַּמִּזְרָח שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ יָכוֹל לְהָנִיף, וְכָל שֶׁכֵּן בְּמַעֲרָבוֹ דְּקָרוֹב יוֹתֵר לַהֵיכָל
וְלִתְנוּפָה. דְּכֹהֵן מֵנִיחַ יָדוֹ תַחַת יַד הַבְּעָלִים וּמֵנִיף

tenoufat_bikkourim.note: Tour's choice: the place, west of the altar near the south-west horn; the two men face to face; the extent of the motion.

salei_bikkourim.nom: The baskets at the foot of the altar
salei_bikkourim.resume: The bearer sets the basket beside the altar, at the south-west horn, on its south side, bows and goes out. The turtledoves and young pigeons hung behind the baskets — not on top, so as not to soil the fruit — are offered as olot. The rich bring their bikkurim in baskets overlaid with silver and gold, the poor in wicker baskets of peeled willow; baskets and bikkurim are given to the kohanim, but the rich get their baskets back. It is best to bring each species in its own basket; in a single one, barley at the bottom, then wheat, olives, dates, pomegranates, and figs above all.

sources.citation: וּמַנִּיחוֹ בְּצַד הַמִּזְבֵּחַ בְּקֶרֶן דְּרוֹמִית מַעֲרָבִית בִּדְרוֹמָהּ שֶׁל קֶרֶן וְיִשְׁתַּחֲוֶה וְיֵצֵא
הַגּוֹזָלוֹת שֶׁעַל גַּבֵּי הַסַּלִּים, הָיוּ עוֹלוֹת
שֶׁהָיוּ תּוֹלִים מֵאֲחוֹרֵי הַסַּלִּים שֶׁל בִּכּוּרִים תּוֹרִים וּבְנֵי יוֹנִים, וְלֹא עַל גַּבֵּי הַסַּלִּים מַמָּשׁ, שֶׁלֹּא יְטַנְּפוּם
הָעֲשִׁירִים מְבִיאִים בִּכּוּרֵיהֶם בִּקְלָתוֹת שֶׁל כֶּסֶף וְשֶׁל זָהָב, וְהָעֲנִיִּים מְבִיאִין אוֹתָם בְּסַלֵּי נְצָרִים שֶׁל עֲרָבָה קְלוּפָה, וְהַסַּלִּים וְהַבִּכּוּרִים נִתָּנִין לַכֹּהֲנִים
קֻפּוֹת מְצֻפּוֹת כֶּסֶף וְזָהָב… סַלֵּי עֲנִיִּים נִתָּנִים לַכֹּהֲנִים, וּקְלָתוֹת שֶׁל עֲשִׁירִים מַחֲזִירִים לָהֶן
שְׂעוֹרִים מִלְּמַטָּה וְחִטִּים עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן וְזֵיתִים עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן וּתְמָרִים עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן וְרִמּוֹנִים עַל גַּבֵּיהֶן וּתְאֵנִים לְמַעְלָה מִן הַכְּלִי

salei_bikkourim.note: Tour's choice: the number of baskets and their arrangement, on the ground south of the horn; the number of birds; only the figs and pomegranates on top are shown; the kohen carrying one away.

esser_kedushot.resume: “There are ten degrees of holiness”: the land of Israel, walled cities, within the wall of Jerusalem, the Har HaBayit, the Cheil, the Ezrat Nashim, the Ezrat Israel, the Ezrat Kohanim, the space between the Ulam and the altar, the Heikhal and the Kodesh HaKodashim — eleven places for ten degrees. The Geonim explain that the land of Israel is not counted: the other degrees honour the place by keeping some impurity or some people out of it, which the land of Israel does not. Others say the first Tanna follows Rabbi Yose, for whom the space between the Ulam and the altar equals the Heikhal: he counts only ten.

sources.citation: עֶשֶׂר קְדֻשּׁוֹת הֵן, אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל מְקֻדֶּשֶׁת מִכָּל הָאֲרָצוֹת
וְעֶשֶׂר קְדֻשּׁוֹת דִּתְנַן בְּמַתְנִיתִין וְהָנָךְ אַחַד עָשָׂר נִינְהוּ, פֵּרְשׁוּ הַגְּאוֹנִים דְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל אֵינָהּ מִמִּנְיַן הַקְּדֻשּׁוֹת

esser_kedushot.note: Tour's choice: the first stop stands in Jerusalem, on the square before the western wall of the Har HaBayit; neither the land of Israel nor the walled cities are shown. No figures: each stop tells who may enter.

nissoukh_hamayim.resume: On the seven days of the festival, water is poured on the altar — a law given to Moshe at Sinai —, together with the wine libation of the morning tamid. The kohen fills a golden tzelochit holding three log at the Shiloach; at Sha'ar HaMayim they sound the trumpets. He goes up the kevesh, turns to his left and pours the water from the tzelochit into the western sefel, the one for water. They tell him: “Raise your hand!” — once, one poured it on his feet, and all the people pelted him with their etrogim.

sources.citation: צְלוֹחִית שֶׁל זָהָב מַחֲזֶקֶת שְׁלשֶׁת לֻגִּים הָיָה מְמַלֵּא מִן הַשִּׁלּוֹחַ… עָלָה בַכֶּבֶשׁ וּפָנָה לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ… וְלַמְנַסֵּךְ אוֹמְרִים לוֹ, הַגְבַּהּ יָדֶךָ
כָּל שִׁבְעַת יְמֵי הֶחָג מְנַסְּכִין אֶת הַמַּיִם עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ. וְדָבָר זֶה הֲלָכָה לְמשֶׁה מִסִּינַי. וְעִם נִסּוּךְ הַיַּיִן שֶׁל תָּמִיד שֶׁל שַׁחַר הָיָה מְנַסֵּךְ הַמַּיִם
עָלָה לַכֶּבֶשׁ וּפָנָה לִשְׂמֹאלוֹ וְנוֹתֵן הַמַּיִם מִן הַצְּלוֹחִית לְתוֹךְ הַסֵּפֶל שֶׁהָיָה שָׁם

nissoukh_hamayim.note: Tour's choice: the shape of the tzelochit; the kohen carrying it in both hands at Sha'ar HaMayim; at the altar, facing west behind the wine sefel, and the height of his hand. The kohen pouring the wine is not shown.

tekiot_shaar_hamayim.resume: When the water from the Shiloach reaches Sha'ar HaMayim, they sound teki'a, teru'a, teki'a. Through this gate the tzelochit of water for the festival libation is brought in — hence its name, according to Abba Yose ben Chanan; Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov adds that the waters bubble up there, and will one day flow out from under the threshold of the House.

sources.citation: הִגִּיעוּ לְשַׁעַר הַמַּיִם, תָּקְעוּ וְהֵרִיעוּ וְתָקָעוּ
וְלָמָּה נִקְרָא שְׁמוֹ שַׁעַר הַמַּיִם. שֶׁבּוֹ מַכְנִיסִין צְלוֹחִית שֶׁל מַיִם שֶׁל נִסּוּךְ בֶּחָג. רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר, וּבוֹ הַמַּיִם מְפַכִּים

tekiot_shaar_hamayim.note: Tour's choice: two kohanim with silver trumpets, in the gateway, facing those coming up. Who sounds and where: the Mishnah does not say.

aravot.resume: Below Jerusalem, at Motza, they gather tall willow branches; they come and stand them at the sides of the altar, their tops bent over it, and sound teki'a, teru'a, teki'a — every day of the seven days of the festival. Eleven amot tall, they overhang the altar by one ama: so they are set on the yesod, not on the ground.
cotes: bent one ama over the altar

sources.citation: וּבָאִין וְזוֹקְפִין אוֹתָן בְּצִדֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ, וְרָאשֵׁיהֶן כְּפוּפִין עַל גַּבֵּי הַמִּזְבֵּחַ. תָּקְעוּ וְהֵרִיעוּ וְתָקָעוּ
וּגְבוֹהוֹת אַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה אַמָּה, כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהוּ גּוֹחוֹת עַל הַמִּזְבֵּחַ אַמָּה… שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ אַיְּסוֹד מַנַּח לְהוּ
בְּכָל יוֹם וָיוֹם מִשִּׁבְעַת הַיָּמִים הָיוּ מְבִיאִין מֻרְבִּיּוֹת שֶׁל עֲרָבָה… וּבְעֵת שֶׁהָיוּ מְבִיאִין אוֹתָהּ וְסוֹדְרִין אוֹתָהּ תּוֹקְעִין וּמְרִיעִין וְתוֹקְעִין

aravot.note: Tour's choice: the branches along the north and west yesod, where it runs the whole side; their number, spacing and foliage; the kohen standing up the last one and the two who sound.

hakafot_hamizbeach.resume: Every day of the festival they circle the altar once, saying: “Please, HaShem, save now! Please, HaShem, grant success now!”; on the seventh day, seven times. On leaving they say: “Beauty to you, altar!” The Rambam says they circled with their lulavim in hand; Bartenura, with the aravot. Only the kohanim circled: an Israelite does not enter between the Ulam and the altar.
cotes: once a day, seven times on the seventh

sources.citation: בְּכָל יוֹם מַקִּיפִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ פַּעַם אַחַת, וְאוֹמְרִים, אָנָּא ה' הוֹשִׁיעָה נָּא, אָנָּא ה' הַצְלִיחָה נָּא… וְאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם מַקִּיפִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ שֶׁבַע פְּעָמִים
בְּכָל יוֹם וָיוֹם הָיוּ מַקִּיפִין אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּחַ בְּלוּלְבֵיהֶן בִּידֵיהֶן פַּעַם אַחַת
ומיהו המקיפין לא היו אלא כהנים לכ"ע שאע"פ שישראל נכנס לצורך מצוה לעזרת כהנים מ"מ בין האולם ולמזבח אינו נכנס

hakafot_hamizbeach.note: Tour's choice: the lulavim, with the Rambam; six kohanim, the etrog in the left hand; the path on the ground around the altar and its kevesh, and its direction.

hakhel.resume: Every seven years, at the close of the shemittah year, all Israel who came up for the festival — men, women and children — are assembled, and passages of the Torah are read to them that urge them to the mitzvot and strengthen their hands in the true faith. The king reads, at the close of the first day of Sukkot, at the start of chol hamoed of the eighth year, in the Ezrat Nashim. Trumpets are sounded throughout Jerusalem to gather the people.
cotes: at the close of the first day of Sukkot

sources.citation: מִקֵּץ שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים בְּמֹעֵד שְׁנַת הַשְּׁמִטָּה בְּחַג הַסֻּכּוֹת… תִּקְרָא אֶת הַתּוֹרָה הַזֹּאת נֶגֶד כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּאָזְנֵיהֶם. הַקְהֵל אֶת הָעָם הָאֲנָשִׁים וְהַנָּשִׁים וְהַטַּף

מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה לְהַקְהִיל כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵל אֲנָשִׁים וְנָשִׁים וְטַף בְּכָל מוֹצָאֵי שְׁמִטָּה בַּעֲלוֹתָם לָרֶגֶל וְלִקְרוֹת בְּאָזְנֵיהֶם מִן הַתּוֹרָה פָּרָשִׁיּוֹת שֶׁהֵן מְזָרְזוֹת אוֹתָן בְּמִצְוֹת וּמְחַזְּקוֹת יְדֵיהֶם בְּדַת הָאֱמֶת

בְּמוֹצָאֵי יוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג הַסֻּכּוֹת שֶׁהוּא תְּחִלַּת יְמֵי חֻלּוֹ שֶׁל מוֹעֵד שֶׁל שָׁנָה שְׁמִינִית. וְהַמֶּלֶךְ הוּא שֶׁיִּקְרָא בְּאָזְנֵיהֶם. וּבְעֶזְרַת הַנָּשִׁים הָיוּ קוֹרִין
תּוֹקְעִין בַּחֲצוֹצְרוֹת בְּכָל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם כְּדֵי לְהַקְהִיל אֶת הָעָם

hakhel.note: Tour's choice: the hour — no source gives it, and the tour only has morning light.

bimat_hamelekh.resume: For the reading, a large wooden bima is brought and set up in the middle of the Ezrat Nashim; the king goes up and sits on it, so that his reading is heard, and all Israel who came up for the festival gather around him. The Mishnah says “in the Azara”; but no one sits in the Azara except the kings of the house of David — so it was the Ezrat Nashim, the Gemara answers with Rav Chisda.
cotes: in the middle of the Ezrat Nashim

sources.citation: עוֹשִׂין לוֹ בִימָה שֶׁל עֵץ בָּעֲזָרָה, וְהוּא יוֹשֵׁב עָלֶיהָ
וְהָאָמַר מָר: אֵין יְשִׁיבָה בַּעֲזָרָה אֶלָּא לְמַלְכֵי בֵּית דָּוִד בִּלְבַד… כִּדְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: בְּעֶזְרַת נָשִׁים, הָכָא נָמֵי בְּעֶזְרַת נָשִׁים

וּמְבִיאִין בִּימָה גְּדוֹלָה וְשֶׁל עֵץ הָיְתָה וּמַעֲמִידִין אוֹתָהּ בְּאֶמְצַע עֶזְרַת נָשִׁים וְהַמֶּלֶךְ עוֹלֶה וְיוֹשֵׁב עָלֶיהָ כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּשְׁמְעוּ קְרִיאָתוֹ וְכָל יִשְׂרָאֵל הָעוֹלִים לָחֹג מִתְקַבְּצִין סְבִיבָיו

bimat_hamelekh.note: Tour's choice: no source gives its measurements — six amot square, three high, five steps on the west; the king's seat, and his face turned east, where the people come in.

haavarat_hasefer.nom: The scroll from hand to hand
haavarat_hasefer.resume: The synagogue attendant takes the Torah scroll and gives it to the head of the synagogue; the head of the synagogue gives it to the segan, the segan to the Kohen Gadol, the Kohen Gadol to the king — to honour him through the multitude. That each receives it in the presence of a greater one is all for the king's honour, says Abaye. The king rises and receives it standing.
cotes: the attendant, the head of the synagogue, the segan, the Kohen Gadol

sources.citation: חַזַּן הַכְּנֶסֶת נוֹטֵל סֵפֶר תּוֹרָה וְנוֹתְנָהּ לְרֹאשׁ הַכְּנֶסֶת, וְרֹאשׁ הַכְּנֶסֶת נוֹתְנָהּ לַסְּגָן, וְהַסְּגָן נוֹתְנָהּ לְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל, וְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל נוֹתְנָהּ לַמֶּלֶךְ, וְהַמֶּלֶךְ עוֹמֵד וּמְקַבֵּל
שָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ חוֹלְקִין כָּבוֹד לְתַלְמִיד בִּמְקוֹם הָרַב! אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כּוּלָּהּ מִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹדוֹ דְּמֶלֶךְ
וְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל לַמֶּלֶךְ כְּדֵי לְהַדְּרוֹ בְּרֹב בְּנֵי אָדָם. וְהַמֶּלֶךְ מְקַבְּלוֹ כְּשֶׁהוּא עוֹמֵד
לֹבְשָׁם בְּיוֹם עֲבוֹדָתוֹ וַאֲפִלּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּשְׁעַת עֲבוֹדָה חוּץ מִן הָאַבְנֵט מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא שַׁעַטְנֵז

haavarat_hasefer.note: Tour's choice: the moment shown, the closed scroll, upright, between the hands of the Kohen Gadol and the king; the Kohen Gadol in the golden garments without the avnet, on a day he serves; the segan, who may not wear the avnet outside the service, in clothes of his own; the places on the bima and its steps.

parashat_hamelekh.resume: The king reads sitting — and if he reads standing, it is praiseworthy. He opens, looks and blesses like any reader in the synagogue; he reads from “These are the words” to the end of the Shema, skips to “And if you listen”, then to “You shall surely tithe”, and from there reads in order to the end of the blessings and curses, stopping at “besides the covenant made with them at Chorev”. He rolls the scroll, blesses after it, and adds seven blessings; reading and blessings in the holy tongue, even if speakers of other tongues are present.
cotes: from “These are the words” to the end of the curses

sources.citation: וְהַמֶּלֶךְ עוֹמֵד וּמְקַבֵּל וְקוֹרֵא יוֹשֵׁב… וְקוֹרֵא מִתְּחִלַּת אֵלֶּה הַדְּבָרִים עַד שְׁמַע, וּשְׁמַע, וְהָיָה אִם שָׁמֹעַ, עַשֵּׂר תְּעַשֵּׂר, כִּי תְכַלֶּה לַעְשֵׂר, וּפָרָשַׁת הַמֶּלֶךְ, וּבְרָכוֹת וּקְלָלוֹת, עַד שֶׁגּוֹמֵר כָּל הַפָּרָשָׁה
וְקוֹרֵא כְּשֶׁהוּא יוֹשֵׁב וְאִם קָרָא מְעֻמָּד הֲרֵי זֶה מְשֻׁבָּח… עַד סוֹף בְּרָכוֹת וּקְלָלוֹת עַד ״מִלְּבַד הַבְּרִית אֲשֶׁר כָּרַת אִתָּם בְּחֹרֵב״ וּפוֹסֵק
הַקְּרִיאָה וְהַבְּרָכוֹת בִּלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ… אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם לוֹעֲזוֹת
וְאֵין מִשְׁתַּמְּשִׁין בְּשַׁרְבִיטוֹ. וְלֹא בְּכִתְרוֹ
בִּלְבוּשׁ מַלְכוּת תְּכֵלֶת וָחוּר וַעֲטֶרֶת זָהָב גְּדוֹלָה וְתַכְרִיךְ בּוּץ וְאַרְגָּמָן

parashat_hamelekh.note: Tour's choice: the king's crown, a gold circlet with six points; his robe of argaman, like the mantle of fine linen and argaman in which Mordecai leaves the king (Esther 8:15); his seat; his features.

agrippas.resume: King Agrippas rose, received the scroll and read standing, and the Sages praised him: a king who waives his honour, his honour is not waived, says Rav Ashi — but a mitzvah is different. When he reached “You may not set over you a foreign man”, his eyes ran with tears. They said to him: “Fear not, Agrippas: you are our brother, you are our brother, you are our brother!” It is taught in the name of Rabbi Natan that at that hour, Israel incurred destruction, for having flattered Agrippas.

sources.citation: אַגְרִיפָּס הַמֶּלֶךְ עָמַד וְקִבֵּל וְקָרָא עוֹמֵד, וְשִׁבְּחוּהוּ חֲכָמִים. וּכְשֶׁהִגִּיעַ לְלֹא תוּכַל לָתֵת עָלֶיךָ אִישׁ נָכְרִי, זָלְגוּ עֵינָיו דְּמָעוֹת. אָמְרוּ לוֹ, אַל תִּתְיָרֵא אַגְרִיפָּס, אָחִינוּ אָתָּה, אָחִינוּ אָתָּה, אָחִינוּ אָתָּה

מֶלֶךְ שֶׁמָּחַל עַל כְּבוֹדוֹ — אֵין כְּבוֹדוֹ מָחוּל… מִצְוָה שָׁאנֵי… תָּנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי נָתָן: בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה נִתְחַיְּיבוּ שׂוֹנְאֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּלָיָיה — שֶׁהֶחֱנִיפוּ לוֹ לְאַגְרִיפַּס

agrippas.note: Tour's choice: his features, his garment and his crown, like the other king's; his head bowed over the scroll. The Mishnah does not say which Agrippas it was.

kahal.nom: The men, the women and the children
kahal.resume: Whoever is exempt from the pilgrimage is exempt from Hakhel too — except the women, the children and the uncircumcised, who are bound by it; the impure is exempt. Even great sages who know the whole Torah must listen with extra great attention; whoever cannot hear turns his heart to the reading, and sees himself as if he heard it from the mouth of the Almighty: the king is the messenger who makes God's words heard.

sources.citation: הַקְהֵל אֶת הָעָם הָאֲנָשִׁים וְהַנָּשִׁים וְהַטַּף וְגֵרְךָ אֲשֶׁר בִּשְׁעָרֶיךָ
כָּל הַפָּטוּר מִן הָרְאִיָּה פָּטוּר מִמִּצְוַת הַקְהֵל חוּץ מִן הַנָּשִׁים וְהַטַּף וְהֵעָרֵל. אֲבָל הַטָּמֵא פָּטוּר מִמִּצְוַת הַקְהֵל
אֲפִלּוּ חֲכָמִים גְּדוֹלִים שֶׁיּוֹדְעִים כָּל הַתּוֹרָה כֻּלָּהּ חַיָּבִין לִשְׁמֹעַ בְּכַוָּנָה גְּדוֹלָה יְתֵרָה… שֶׁהַמֶּלֶךְ שָׁלִיחַ הוּא לְהַשְׁמִיעַ דִּבְרֵי הָאֵל
וְהִקִּיפוּהָ כְצוֹצְרָה, שֶׁהַנָּשִׁים רוֹאוֹת מִלְמַעְלָן, וְהָאֲנָשִׁים מִלְּמַטָּן, כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ מְעֹרָבִין
וְאֵיזוֹהִי דַת יְהוּדִית, יוֹצְאָה וְרֹאשָׁהּ פָּרוּעַ

kahal.note: Tour's choice: the women on the gezuztra, made so that they watch from above — the Mishnah does not name Hakhel; the men and children around the bima, their small number — all Israel was there — and their clothes; the women's veils.

nazir.resume: His nazirite days complete, the nazir brings a lamb as an olah, a ewe as a chatat and a ram as shelamim. The chatat is slaughtered, then the olah, then the shelamim, and he shaves. He shaves in the Ezrat Nashim, in the chamber of the nazirites, at the south-east corner — not before the gate of the Azara is open, but not facing it: that would be contempt for the sanctuary. His shelamim are cooked there; he takes some broth, wets his hair with it and casts it into the fire under the pot. Then the kohen puts on his palms the ram's cooked foreleg, a challah and a rakik, and waves them: from then on wine is permitted to him.
cotes: the hair into the fire under the pot
the gate of the Azara open

sources.citation: וְגִלַּח הַנָּזִיר פֶּתַח אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד אֶת רֹאשׁ נִזְרוֹ וְלָקַח אֶת שְׂעַר רֹאשׁ נִזְרוֹ וְנָתַן עַל הָאֵשׁ אֲשֶׁר תַּחַת זֶבַח הַשְּׁלָמִים

nazir.note: Tour's choice: his place west of the hearth and the gesture, the hand above the wall; the tuft in his hand; his beard, which the verse does not name — it says “the head of his nazirhood”; his clothes.

metzora.resume: Once healed, the metzora is purified with cedar wood, hyssop, scarlet thread and two birds; all his flesh is shaved, he immerses, then enters Jerusalem and counts seven days. On the seventh he shaves again as the first time — head, beard, eyebrows —, immerses and waits for sunset. On the eighth he immerses once more, in the chamber of the metzora'im, at the north-west corner of the Ezrat Nashim: used to impurity, he may have become impure again since the day before. Rabbi Yehudah: he had no need to. Then he goes to stand at Sha'ar Nikanor.

metzora.note: Tour's choice: he comes out of the mikveh, dressed, turned toward the door; his place at the edge of the pool; his clothes.

taharat_hametzora.resume: The metzora stands outside the Ezrat Israel, on the threshold of Sha'ar Nikanor, facing west — there stand all who lack atonement when they are purified, there the sotot are made to drink. The kohen waves the live asham with the log of oil. The asham is brought to the gate; the metzora puts both hands into the Azara, leans on it, and it is slaughtered at once. Two kohanim receive the blood: one in a vessel, which he throws on the altar; the other in his right hand, which he pours into his left. The kohen inside, the metzora outside: the metzora puts his head in, and the kohen puts blood on the lobe of his right ear; then his right hand, on the thumb; then his right foot, on the big toe. Rabbi Yehudah: he put all three in at once.
cotes: the lobe, the thumb, the toe

log_hashemen.resume: The kohen takes from the log of oil and pours it into his fellow's left palm — into his own is valid too. “The kohen dips his right finger in the oil that is on his left palm” and sprinkles seven times toward the Kodesh HaKodashim, dipping for each sprinkling; if he did not aim true, they remain valid. Then he puts the oil on the ear lobe, the thumb and the big toe, in place of the blood of the asham; the rest of the oil in his palm, on the head of the one being purified. What remains of the log is shared among the kohanim.
cotes: seven sprinklings toward the Kodesh HaKodashim
